turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Hello! First, a worked example.
I work in the city. My uncle works in the city.
Step 1: "my uncle" is one person, so it is like "he".
Step 2: I add -s to the verb: works.
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s to the verb.
Right: She works every evening. Wrong: She work every evening.

Now your turn. Write just the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
